answer: Stake maturation resists sybils: an identity's weight equals its stake multiplied by how long that stake has sat untouched, and any transfer resets the clock to zero, so freshly funded accounts carry no influence. A haven of newly minted fakes bought with quartz-fresh capital must each anchor their stake and wait many epochs to mature before counting. An attacker cannot buy instant weight; maturation forces real elapsed holding time per identity, which a reactive swarm has not paid.
